items.headline: Fast but error-prone AI assists in solving a decades-old fluid mechanics problem in five weeks
items.excerpt: An AI assistant helped University of Colorado Boulder researchers crack a mathematical problem their lab had wrestled with for a year and a half, in five weeks. It also made subtle errors along the way, exposing both the promise and the limits of AI as a research partner.

items.headline: AI can complement traditional weather models by offering guidance on tropical cyclones several days before they form
items.excerpt: A new study of Atlantic tropical cyclone forecasts finds AI models can flag when and where tropical disturbances may spin up into storms days before conventional physics models do — useful extra guidance rather than a replacement.

items.headline: AI decodes DNA initiator sequence found in about 60% of human genes
items.excerpt: Researchers used machine learning to decode an initiator element that governs gene activation in roughly 60% of human genes, a regulatory grammar that had resisted decades of manual analysis.

items.headline: AI doesn't just play better chess — it manages complexity differently
items.excerpt: Chess engines beat grandmasters, but a new analysis asks how their play actually differs. The answer is less about raw calculation than about how machines steer positions toward complexity humans find hard to hold.

items.headline: Researchers develop AI framework to optimize solid oxide electrolysis cell operation
items.excerpt: A Korean team built an AI-guided optimization framework that slashes the computation needed to tune solid oxide electrolysis cell operating conditions, replacing brute-force simulation sweeps with learned surrogates.

items.headline: DigBat: An AI-ready digital platform for solid-state battery research
items.excerpt: Solid-state electrolyte data is scattered across papers in incompatible formats. DigBat restructures that literature into a machine-readable platform so ML models can actually train on decades of battery research.

items.headline: Students find AI isn't a cure-all for drug discovery
items.excerpt: Companies are pouring billions into AI-driven drug research. A Northeastern student project put the tools to the test and found the hard parts of discovery stubbornly resistant to automation.

items.headline: Looking beyond natural sequences: a machine-learning framework for protein design
items.excerpt: MIT biologists built a machine-learning framework that raises the hit rate of computational protein design while pushing models away from simply regurgitating sequences that already exist in nature.

items.headline: Generating scenarios for extreme events, without extreme data
items.excerpt: MIT engineers built a model that predicts plausible worst-case scenarios — an extreme storm's likely duration, intensity and footprint — without needing past examples of the extreme event itself.

items.headline: AI Spots Hidden Solar Storm Signs 9 Hours Early
items.excerpt: A machine-learning model reading subtle magnetic precursors in solar observations flags coming solar storms up to nine hours before current space-weather methods, buying satellite and grid operators real lead time.

items.headline: FAU Researchers Use Quantum Machine Learning to Predict Heart Disease
items.excerpt: FAU researchers report a quantum machine learning model that hit 90.26% accuracy predicting heart disease across data from 918 patients — an early, concrete test of QML on clinical tabular data.

items.headline: Researchers Use IBM Quantum Computer to Test Drug-Docking Method
items.excerpt: A hybrid quantum-classical molecular docking method ran on an IBM quantum processor, showing a resource-efficient path for quantum hardware to contribute to structure-based drug design.

items.headline: Improved QLEDs with machine learning
items.excerpt: Machine learning searched solvent formulation space to find recipes that yield unusually homogeneous quantum dot films, a direct materials-processing win for display engineering.

items.headline: AI models flub these intelligence tests. Can you fare any better?
items.excerpt: Puzzles and games keep exposing gaps in what frontier models actually understand. MIT Technology Review lays out seven tests readers can try against the machines.

items.headline: Piloting the world's first double-blind AI evaluations
items.excerpt: DeepMind is piloting double-blind evaluation of AI systems, borrowing clinical-trial methodology so benchmark results can't be gamed by labs grading their own homework.
